newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds modestly off, spreads narrow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds modestly off, spreads narrow.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities displayed modest losses in relatively thin trading Wednesday, mortgage experts said.
Spreads over Treasuries held unchanged to a touch narrower, traders said. "They're doing pretty well, just a tick or two tighter," a Ginnie Mae trader said.
In pass-throughs, conventionals narrowly edged out Ginnie Maes in many coupons, largely because of collection for a Fannie Mae deal, traders said.
"(Ginnies) are underperforming conventionals," one trader said. "There's a big callable deal getting done."
In key issues, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0-percent paper was unchanged at 100-18/32, yielding 118 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 1/32 lower, at 100-18/32 and 101-25/32, respectively.
Five-year Treasuries were off 3/32 at 6.78 percent, and 10-year notes were off 3/32 at 6.89 percent.
A surprisingly robust industrial output report set the negative tone in the fixed-income market, analysts said.
It showed industry activity up 0.9 percent in March against a 0.6 percent rise in February. Economists in a Reuters poll had projected a 0.6 percent increase.
Perhaps more troubling, capacity utilization grew to 84.1 percent, compared with 83.6 percent the month before.

"It does prove what Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan was worried about: that we are bumping up against capacity that could be inflationary," said Astrid Adolfson, first vice president and an economist at MCM MoneyWatch Inc."
